title: Advent customs
hookLine: a tree of ornaments telling the story from creation to Christ

lines: A BARE BRANCH IN A POT OF STONES.
FROM THE GARDEN TO THE MANGER.
cards: Early December. A bare branch stands in a pot of stones on the dining table. No lights, no tinsel.
Each evening after dinner, a child is allowed to hang one homemade ornament on it, and someone reads a short passage from the Bible. A paper apple. A tiny wooden boat.
A ram cut out of felt. A ladder made of popsicle sticks. A coat with too many colors.
By Christmas the branch is crowded, and anyone who sat at that table has heard a whole story, a few minutes a night, from the garden to the manger.

teach.h: A ROD OUT OF THE ROOT OF JESSE.
teach.b: The name comes from Isaiah, in the Douay-Rheims: "And there shall come forth a rod out of the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise up out of his root." An old root, and out of it, something new and green.
Christians read that shoot as the Messiah, growing from the family line of David. So who's Jesse? Not a king.
In the first book of Samuel he's a man of Bethlehem with a house full of sons, and his youngest is out minding the sheep when the prophet comes looking for a king. That youngest boy is David.
So the prophecy reaches back behind the king, to an ordinary household in Bethlehem.
Matthew's Gospel names him in the long genealogy at its very start: "And Obed begot Jesse. And Jesse begot David the king." Then, the ornaments.
Each one stands for a person or a moment in that family story.
A piece of fruit, for Adam and Eve; Genesis never says it was an apple. A boat, for Noah. A ram, for Abraham and Isaac.

teach.h: A FLOWER SHALL RISE UP OUT OF HIS ROOT.
teach.b: A coat, for Joseph. Families choose their own sets, so no two Jesse trees look quite the same. Last, why Advent, the season of waiting you met in your first year.
The Jesse tree shows what the waiting was made of: generations of people, some flawed, some surprising, gathered on one branch as the story that leads to Jesus, read aloud one name at a time.

how: Some Catholic families, schools and parishes keep a Jesse tree in Advent: a branch or small tree on which an ornament is hung each day, each standing for a figure or story from the Bible, with a short reading.

games.q: the prophet comes to Jesse's house looking for a king, and Jesse's sons are brought out one by one. who is chosen?
o: the eldest, who looks every inch a king.
none of them; the prophet leaves.
the youngest, who was out minding the sheep.
games.why: it's David, the youngest, called in from the sheep. the tree reaches back behind the king to his father's ordinary house.

practice: Choose one Bible story you remember, Noah, Ruth, David with his sling, Mary at the door, and ask what small object would stand for it: a boat, a sheaf of wheat, a stone. Hold that image until it's clear.
If you pray, plan to read that story again tonight; if you don't, simply let the picture stay with you.

wordCard.voice: Jesse tree. An Advent branch hung with ornaments, one a night, telling the story of Jesus's family line, named for Isaiah's rod out of the root of Jesse. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew, Jesse: the name in Isaiah's line about the root.
